Subject: PoC next steps & deployment mode (recap from today's call)

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan.

Call summary:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood for document ingestion+Q&A in Acme's customer support workflow (aim to reduce handle time and deflect common questions).
- Primary constraints: 99% of data must stay in VPC, strict audit logging, SOC2 controls, and predictable latency < 300ms for short queries.
- Expected volume: steady-state ~15 requests/sec with spiky bursts to 50 rps.

Deployment mode options we discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest to get started, lower ops burden, but would require additional contractual controls for data residency and may not meet your VPC requirement.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools in our cloud with network peering and stricter isolation. Good middle ground for predictable throughput and SLA.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full customer-managed VPC or on-prem box, recommended if you require all traffic to stay in your network and for strict compliance.

Recommended PoC approach (proposed):
- PoC objective: validate latency at 99th pctl < 300ms, embedding/recall accuracy on 10k support docs, and KV caching effectiveness to reduce token cost by at least 35%.
- Duration: 4 weeks technical PoC + 2 weeks evaluation.
- Stakeholders: Alex (Product), Engineering (network lead), Security/Compliance, and Procurement for contract prep.
- Deliverables: test harness, sample workload, SLO runbook, and a short results deck.

Can you confirm: (a) whether Acme prefers Dedicated capacity or Private VPC for the PoC, (b) the right engineering contact for peering/network, and (c) if procurement should be looped on the initial contract draft?

Attaching a brief PoC SOW and network checklist for your team to review.

Thanks,
—Marissa

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the SOW. Useful. Quick answers below: 

1) Deployment mode: our security team leans toward Dedicated capacity for the PoC — we want isolation and predictable perf without the full lift of private on-prem for the initial evaluation. If the PoC goes well, we may request a Private VPC for production.

2) Network/peering contact: looping in Samir Patel (engineering) on this thread — he will own setting up peering and running the network checklist.

3) Procurement: yes please loop procurement early. I've cc'd procurement@acme-corp.com on this reply. They typically want an initial 60-day review window and standard liability clauses.

Success criteria: we agree with your suggested metrics. A couple of additions: 1) average token cost per query target to be <= $0.02, and 2) evaluation on a 200-user concurrent simulation for burst behaviour.

Samir and procurement team — can you confirm availability for a kickoff next Wed (6/16) or Thurs (6/17)?

Thanks,
